summary: Packaged the built-in service recovery workflow as a core workflow-pack artifact bound to AgentCore service recovery and local-only replay.
acceptance_evidence: workflow-service-recovery.json declares coordinate agentos:workflow-pack/agentos/service-recovery@1.0.0 and core trust tier.
The workflow pack depends on agentos:policy-pack/agentos/core-policy@1.0.0 with missing_behavior=block-activation and no host mutation fallback.
workflow.plan_spec_owner is AgentCore and restart_action_tool is svc.restart.
Activation requires AgentCore PlanSpec, SecurityExecutionEngine, exact approval, replay evidence and compatibility evidence.
registry-snapshot.json points the service recovery coordinate to file:///etc/agentos/ecosystem/core/workflow-service-recovery.json.
validate-alpha-rootfs.ps1 now treats the service recovery workflow manifest as a required rootfs artifact.
functional-capability-replay.ps1 checks the built-in workflow pack alongside existing service recovery tests.

commands.summary: 5 AgentCore service recovery tests passed, including denied path with no restart effect.
Functional replay passed 9/9 capability checks, including built-in ecosystem packs.
Alpha rootfs validation passed 11/11 required artifacts, including ecosystem.workflow_service_recovery.
Workspace tests passed: agent_core 107, agentd 58, runtime_contracts 23, security_execution 79 plus doctests.

blocked_shortcuts: The workflow pack does not execute shell directly.
svc.restart remains an exact-approval semantic tool action.
Denied restart paths do not prepare effects.
The workflow cannot activate when the core policy dependency is missing.
promotion_impact: AgentOS now has a built-in service recovery workflow-pack that can be activated only through the AgentCore and SecurityExecution activation chain.
